generated_report: Atelectasis refers to the collapse or closure of a lung resulting in reduced or absent gas exchange. It may affect part or all of one lung. It's a condition often seen in patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). Consolidation refers to the process by which the lung becomes filled with liquid instead of air, often due to infection or inflammation. Pulmonary edema is a condition caused by excess fluid in the lungs, which can result from heart conditions or other causes. Pleural effusion is the build-up of excess fluid between the layers of the pleura outside the lungs.
